title: When I Am Only a Dream | A Poem by Paramahansa Yogananda Read by Sri Daya Mata
formattedMarkdown:
# When I Am Only a Dream

### A Sacred Recitation by Sri Daya Mata
*Self-Realization Fellowship / Yogoda Satsanga Society of India*

In the spiritual history of the world, few texts carry the profound, comforting assurance of a Guru’s eternal presence as beautifully as the immortal poem, "When I Am Only a Dream," written by Paramahansa Yogananda. Recited with exquisite devotion and maternal tenderness by His beloved disciple and third president of Self-Realization Fellowship, Sri Daya Mata, this reading serves as a timeless bridge between the visible and the invisible worlds. It is a divine message of hope, reminding us that the bond between the Guru and the true disciple transcends the boundaries of physical life and death.

### The Eternal Covenant of the Guru’s Presence

When a great Master departs from the physical plane, devotees often feel a profound sense of grief and separation. Yet, Paramahansa Yogananda repeatedly assured His followers that He would be closer to them after He left His physical form than He was during His lifetime. "When I Am Only a Dream" is His eternal covenant of love, a poetic testament that His guiding hand, His protective gaze, and His unconditional love remain fully accessible to anyone who seeks Him in the silent temple of the soul. 

Sri Daya Mata, who spent more than twenty years in the close presence of the Master, brings a unique depth of realization to these verses. Her voice, saturated with the peace of God and the joy of her own attunement, breathes life into every line, turning the poem into a living transmission of spiritual power.

> "I shall wake from my physical sleep to tell you that I am not gone; that I am ever with you, watching over you with eyes of love."

Through these words, the Master reminds us that our earthly life itself is but a passing dream. When His physical form becomes a dream to us, we must learn to awaken to the greater, eternal reality where He is ever-present in the light of God. He is not gone; He has merely stepped behind the screen of nature, waiting for us to peer through the veil of delusion.

### The Whisper in the Silence of Meditation

For the seeker on the path of Kriya Yoga, the primary way to experience the Guru’s presence is through deep, interiorized meditation. When we quiet the turbulent waves of our thoughts and feelings, we begin to perceive the subtle manifestations of His spirit. The Master did not ask us to worship His physical body, but rather to attune our consciousness to the Infinite Spirit that spoke through Him.

> "When you can no longer see my physical form, look for me in the temple of your silent meditation, in the quietness of your mind."

In the depths of stillness, when the breath becomes calm and the heart is quiet, the Guru whispers His guidance. He speaks to us not through audible words, but through intuitive perception, gentle urges of the soul, and sudden flashes of spiritual understanding. By developing this inner receptive state, we realize that His wisdom is active, dynamic, and ever-present to guide our steps.

### Seeking the Divine Beloved Beyond Form

Paramahansa Yogananda always pointed His disciples toward the ultimate goal of life: union with the Divine Mother, the Lord of the Universe. He explained that the Guru is a transparent medium, a clear window through which the light of God shines upon the seeker. When we love the Guru, we are loving God; and when we feel the Guru’s love, we are feeling the tender embrace of the Divine Mother.

In "When I Am Only a Dream," the Master encourages us to look for Him in all beautiful things—in the sunset, in the stars, in the perfume of the flowers, and in the noble impulses of our own hearts. By expanding our consciousness to see His presence in all creation, we break down the barriers of ego and limitation, stepping into the vastness of the Christ Consciousness that He embodied.

> "Look for me in the noble deeds of your life, in the love you give to all, and in the selfless service you perform for your brothers and sisters."

### Practical Habits to Attune with the Guru’s Presence

To bridge the gap between our daily life and the silent presence of the Guru, Sri Daya Mata and the senior monastics of Self-Realization Fellowship recommend several practical spiritual habits:

*   **Daily Silent Meditation:** Dedicate time each morning and evening to sit in deep stillness, practicing the Kriya Yoga techniques faithfully. End your meditation by mentally conversing with the Guru, offering your devotion and listening for His response in your heart.
*   **Mental Whispering and Prayer:** Practice "mental whispering" throughout the day. Talk to the Guru as a living, loving friend. Share your joys, your struggles, and your questions, trusting that He hears every whisper.
*   **Study His Sacred Writings:** Read from *Autobiography of a Yogi*, *Whispers from Eternity*, or other teachings daily. Immersing your mind in His words is a powerful way to align your thoughts with His consciousness.
*   **Serve Others Selflessly:** Keep your heart open by serving others without expecting anything in return. The Master’s spirit is especially active where there is love, compassion, and selfless service.
*   **Keep His Picture in Your Sacred Space:** Having a dedicated altar with a picture of the Master helps focus your attention and serves as a constant physical reminder of His ever-living presence.

### A Sacred Benediction and Blessing

As we absorb the profound vibrations of this sacred poem, let us close our eyes and feel the loving presence of Paramahansa Yogananda and the tender, maternal blessing of Sri Daya Mata surrounding us. Let us pray that we may ever remain faithful to the spiritual path, growing daily in devotion, peace, and love for God.

*O Divine Mother, Heavenly Father, Friend, Beloved God, and Great Gurus: May Thy love shine forever on the sanctuary of our devotion, and may we find Thy guiding hand in every circumstance of our lives. When we walk through the dark valleys of life, remind us that Thou art always with us, and that our Beloved Guru is but a whisper away, guiding us back to Thy eternal home of light and joy.*

*Jai Guru. Jai Ma.*
